races.name: Visit Perth Museum Maiden Hurdle Race (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Biggles
runners_data.note: A nine-year-old veteran whose best recent hurdle form (2nd/16f/Good) aligns with today's conditions; Stan Sheppard partners him for Tom Lacey and his prominent style means he should track the front-runners cleanly — the concern is age and a patchy recent record including a poor run last time.

runners_data.name: Hawthorn Road
runners_data.note: 93 days off the track for Iain Jardine is notable, and all three hurdle starts came on Soft ground — Good conditions are unproven for this genuine hold-up horse; the headgear notation (hood) adds a further question mark on first run back.

runners_data.name: St Just In Time
runners_data.note: Harry Derham's charge showed a placed effort on Good ground (3rd/15f) and has decent hurdling form, but it's a natural hold-up horse that will find itself racing in a more forward position than it prefers given the hold-up congestion in this field, which tempers its winning chance under this race shape.

runners_data.name: C'Est Pour Moi
runners_data.note: The four-year-old front-runner is ridden by a 7lb claimer and both hurdle runs have come on Good ground — in theory the conditions suit — but a rating of 120 for a horse placed zero times in two hurdle starts suggests it is on a retrieval mission and could struggle if Crackalackin matches it stride for stride early.

runners_data.name: Crackalackin
runners_data.note: A consistent Good-ground performer with two placed efforts at exactly this trip (2m/16f/Good), Luke Scott's 3lb claim is useful; the lowered OR of 100 versus rivals rated 120 leaves it well-treated on paper and its front-running style is the most natural match for the pace scenario in this race.

runners_data.name: Tracker Issue
runners_data.note: Ryan Mania is a high-quality booking for a hold-up horse with limited form (one start over hurdles, sixth of six last time); 22 days since that run is not a concern, but the horse must find improvement quickly and will need a trouble-free passage from a genuine hold-up berth that is already crowded.

runners_data.name: Try Them
runners_data.note: Brian Hughes is a major positive for Patrick Neville's four-year-old, who has a solid recent placed effort (2nd/16f/Good) that directly mirrors today's conditions; a prominent style suits the projected race shape perfectly, and the step back from Soft to Good may actually help based on its best form.

races.paceDynamic: C'Est Pour Moi and Crackalackin are the two confirmed front-runners in a seven-runner field, and with both likely to contest the early lead from the gates, this race will be run at an honest, genuine gallop from the outset over Perth's 2m trip on Good ground. C'Est Pour Moi, ridden by an amateur claimer, may be slightly more vulnerable to being pressured, while Crackalackin has shown consistent prominence in similar Good-ground hurdles and is unlikely to concede the rail cheaply. The resulting pace should be genuine rather than suicidal, producing a race that will test stamina but also allow those tracking in behind to conserve energy through the middle section. This shape most favours prominent racers or those tracking just off the speed — Biggles and Try Them — who can travel into contention without burning fuel in a front-running battle they never started. The field holds more hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear; St Just In Time is a genuine hold-up horse shown in midfield due to the redistribution, meaning Hawthorn Road and Tracker Issue are also competing for the same late-running territory, making a clean run from the back harder to guarantee.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Honest Gallop, Tracker Types Win
scenarios.trigger: If C'Est Pour Moi and Crackalackin set a genuine contested pace and the leaders tie each other up, allowing prominent chasers to pounce turning in.
scenarios.body: Biggles and Try Them, tracking in the first three on Good ground that suits both, are ideally placed to inherit the lead when the front-runners stop; Brian Hughes's positional judgment on Try Them in particular could prove decisive if he slots into second or third early.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Outstays Field
scenarios.trigger: If Crackalackin or C'Est Pour Moi builds a decisive lead without being seriously pressured and controls the tempo to grind rivals into submission.
scenarios.body: On Good ground over 2m at Perth, a front-runner dictating a measured pace can be almost impossible to reel in, especially if rivals lack the cruising speed to close; Crackalackin's consistent Good-ground form and three placed efforts at this trip make it the more likely of the two to steal this way.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Deliver
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is hot enough to burn out all prominent horses and the race truly falls apart in the straight.
scenarios.body: St Just In Time has genuine hold-up ability and decent form at 2m on similar ground, and a true end-to-end gallop could leave the late finishers with ground to make up — but this scenario is undermined by the fact that Hawthorn Road and Tracker Issue are also genuine hold-up types competing for the same closing berths.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Messy Pace, Midfield Benefits
scenarios.trigger: If early position is contested chaotically and the race loses shape, turning the 2m into a scramble.
scenarios.body: A chaotic race over this trip on Good ground at Perth occasionally produces a mid-division winner who avoids early trouble and picks up a clean run; Biggles, versatile and with form at the track, could capitalise if the front-runners disrupt each other severely.

watchPoints.text: C'Est Pour Moi and Crackalackin — watch which of the two front-runners dominates for position at the first hurdle, as the loser of that battle may drop away quickly and compromise those immediately behind them.

Hawthorn Road — 93 days off the track, all hurdle form on Soft, hood retained; if it jumps poorly or needs the run, Dylan Johnston may struggle to get it competitive from a hold-up berth on Good ground.

St Just In Time — forced to race further forward than its natural style allows due to hold-up congestion; if it can't settle in its adjusted position, it risks pulling hard and emptying before the straight.

Try Them — watch whether Brian Hughes positions it in the first three early; if he elects to drop it out and ride a waiting race, it moves against this race's projected shape and its chance diminishes significantly.

Tracker Issue — only six career starts over hurdles with limited exposed form; watch the market move at declarations and early betting, as any gamble would suggest Mania has been given confident instructions about this horse's well-being and readiness.

races.name: QuinnBet Novices' Limited Handicap Steeple Chase (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Tamarind Bay
runners_data.note: Back-to-back wins on Good ground over 2m and 2m2f give him solid claims at this trip; Sean Bowen partners a horse in fine form for trainer Mickey Bowen, and his prominent racing style means he is ideally placed to inherit the lead if Follow Your Luck fades.
runners_data.comment: Tamarind Bay arrives here on the back of back-to-back wins and, with experience of today's trip and going, he has every reason to be competitive off a 48-day break; our rating makes him the clear pick of this five-runner field.

runners_data.name: Follow Your Luck
runners_data.note: The tactical linchpin of this race — a confirmed front-runner who sets the shape for everyone else; the 177-day layoff is the single biggest risk factor, as Patrick Neville's record of 0/5 runners in the last 14 days suggests limited recent runners, and fitness on return is the key question.
runners_data.comment: Follow Your Luck arrives on the back of three wins in his last four starts, including a hat-trick of victories, and has run over today's trip before; carrying 160 lb fresh off a 177-day absence are the questions connections must answer.

runners_data.name: Glen To Glen
runners_data.note: Has headgear (p) fitted and holds some promise as a young 4-year-old, but recent form reads 710-5R and his best Going performances have come at shorter trips; Kielan Woods will need him to travel sweetly from the back, which is a big ask given his inconsistency.
runners_data.comment: Landed a win four starts back and has experience of today's going, with 152 lb no bar to a bold showing at a rating of 128 — the main concern is that refusal last time out, which must be forgiven if he is to play a leading role here.

runners_data.name: Ras Kassar
runners_data.note: Headgear (ht) fitted and ran creditably when second over 2m on Good going 20 days ago, so fitness is not a concern; David Pipe's runner races prominently and handles this surface, though his OR of 111 leaves him with plenty to find against the better-handicapped rivals.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked last on our figures, Ras Kassar faces a stiff task under 147 lb, though he has run over today's trip and going before and was second last time out.

runners_data.name: Kinbara Firstdraft
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old who races from hold-up, has shown willing on Good ground before (1W2P from 9 runs in similar conditions), but his form string of 4-5745 indicates a horse that fills the places without threatening to win; Derek Fox will look for a clean round rather than fireworks.
runners_data.comment: Kinbara Firstdraft has run over today's trip and going, arrives here 34 days fresh, and a rating of 126 has him fourth of the five on our figures; yet to score in his last five starts, and that stubborn winless streak remains the key concern.

races.paceDynamic: Follow Your Luck is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no other genuine pace-setter to challenge him, Brian Hughes will control tempo from the outset over this 2m4f trip on Good ground. Tamarind Bay and Ras Kassar will press from prominent positions, but neither is a natural leader who will disrupt Follow Your Luck's rhythm, meaning the pace is likely to be honest rather than blistering — precisely the kind of metronomic gallop that suits a horse with stamina and a clean jumping round. Glen To Glen and Kinbara Firstdraft are both hold-up types who will need something to go wrong up front to get involved late. This race shape strongly favours hold-up and prominent horses with superior stamina who can outstay a regulated pace, but the single uncontested leader is the biggest tactical beneficiary if he jumps well and his fitness after 177 days off holds.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Follow Your Luck Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Follow Your Luck jumps fluently and dictates an uncontested, measured pace throughout.
scenarios.body: Hughes sets a comfortable gallop that no rival has the mandate or inclination to seriously challenge, and the 5-year-old's front-running profile means he arrives at the final fences full of running with rivals having used energy chasing him.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Follow Your Luck weakens through race-fitness concerns after 177 days off and is swallowed by the chasing pack.
scenarios.body: Tamarind Bay, coming off back-to-back wins on Good ground and ridden by Sean Bowen, looms as the primary beneficiary as a prominent tracker who can assert from 3 out; Ras Kassar, with recent course experience over 2m on Good, also picks up ground.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is genuinely strong and the field strings out, creating enough attrition for closers to swoop.
scenarios.body: Glen To Glen would need a complete turnaround on recent disappointing form and would have to produce a career-best effort at this trip; Kinbara Firstdraft has placed on Good ground before but his consistent mid-pack finishes suggest he lacks the finishing burst to win off this OR.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Jumping Error Reshuffles
scenarios.trigger: If a key faller or series of jumping errors among the leaders dramatically fragments the race in the final mile.
scenarios.body: A small five-runner field means any incident has outsized impact, and hold-up horses Glen To Glen or Kinbara Firstdraft could inherit a position they could never have earned through raw ability; neither has the form profile to win cleanly but chaos is a genuine equaliser.

watchPoints.text: Follow Your Luck — monitor his jumping and early jumping confidence; a stumble or hesitation at the first few fences after 177 days off could unravel the entire race shape and hand control to Tamarind Bay.

Tamarind Bay — watch whether Sean Bowen elects to push up and pressure Follow Your Luck or sit a length or two off; if he applies early pressure, the pace quickens and hold-up horses gain marginal relevance.

Glen To Glen — the refusal (R) on latest run is a significant jumping flag in a steeplechase; if he makes a serious error or unseats Kielan Woods, the five-runner field is immediately thinned and race dynamics shift.

Ras Kassar — 20 days since last run and headgear fitted; watch whether Dylan Johnston pushes to go with Tamarind Bay early or settles for the rear of the prominent group, as his positioning in the first mile will determine whether he can get competitive late.

races.name: IM Group Handicap Hurdle Race

runners_data.name: Lets Mingle
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner for Lucinda Russell/Michael Scudamore, uncontested lead is the key asset here; three wins from six Good-ground runs and a recent win 34 days ago on Good keeps confidence high, though STYLE_FIT tag is irrelevant here as the prominent map position undersells how naturally this horse wants to lead.
runners_data.comment: Lets Mingle arrives in fine form, winning last time out and recording a third three starts back, and she has experience over today's distance and going. A 34-day break looks no concern, and 168 lb is the only mild query on her profile.

runners_data.name: Harry
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old prominent racer for David Pipe; two wins in recent form (25/711), handles a range of going, and Rian Corcoran's 5lb claim is a meaningful weight relief — straightforward tactical profile suits a steady-pace scenario where he can sit close to Lets Mingle throughout.

runners_data.name: Summergrounds
runners_data.note: Veteran ten-year-old for Nicky Richards, races prominently and has nine runs from fifteen on similar going yielding one win and seven places — model of consistency; Danny McMenamin takes the mount and the distance looks fine, though the lack of a recent win may tell against him in a tight finish.
runners_data.comment: Summergrounds showed a glimpse of his best when third two starts back, has run over today's trip and going, and our rating of 112 marks him as a genuine threat from a field of ten; the main risk is that pulled-up run three starts back, which clouds his reliability.

runners_data.name: Dream's Ka
runners_data.note: Young four-year-old hold-up racer for Katie Scott with an outstanding Good-ground record: six from ten on similar conditions including two wins in last five runs; Ryan Mania rides and the 22-day turnaround is fine — the danger is whether the pace is slow enough to enable a late run.
runners_data.comment: Won two starts back and has run over today's trip and going, so the conditions hold no fears; but he was beaten into eighth last time out and his rating of 107 ranks him fifth of ten, leaving plenty to do at 163 lb.

runners_data.name: Cosmic Soul
runners_data.note: Brian Hughes partners this six-year-old who owns four wins from eleven Good-ground runs, all on similar surfaces; returned 0 from last run (69-day absence is a mild flag) but the progressive winning sequence before that (1-1-1-1) commands respect — needs cover from just off the pace.
runners_data.comment: Cosmic Soul won three of his last five starts, including back-to-back victories two and three runs back, but flopped last time out and returns after 69 days off; he has experience of today's trip and conditions, though 160 lb is a significant burden to shoulder.

runners_data.name: Garde Des Champs
runners_data.note: Consistent ten-year-old hold-up performer with thirteen runs from fifteen on Good/similar, though only one win; Gregor Walkingshaw's 10lb claim helps offset the weight, and the tongue-strap/cheekpieces combo suggests connections are trying to sharpen a horse that keeps running into places rather than winning.
runners_data.comment: Garde Des Champs has been a model of consistency, finishing second last time out and third in two of his three starts before that, and our rating of 114 marks him out as the pick of this field; the concern is he remains yet to win in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Follow Charlie
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up type who won over 2m on Good last time out (34 days ago) for R Mike Smith, whose stable has a 1/13 in the last 14 days; trainer form is modest but Follow Charlie's own form over similar going (4/15, two wins) suggests the horse finds its best at the right moment.
runners_data.comment: Follow Charlie won last time out and has run over today's trip and going, giving him relevant experience, but he carries 160 lb and is ranked seventh of ten in the field, suggesting he faces a stiff ask to follow up.

runners_data.name: O'Faolains Glory
runners_data.note: A natural prominent racer pushed into the midfield map position because the field is overloaded with pace-seeking types; 146-day absence is a significant concern and all five sim-going runs returned no wins — if it does push forward from an unfavourable position, stamina late in the race is the question.
runners_data.comment: A 146-day absence and a heavy burden of 159 lb make O'Faolains Glory hard to fancy on her return, and she is ranked ninth of ten on our figures; she has run over today's trip and going before, and two wins in her last five starts hint at ability worth monitoring once she gets fit.

runners_data.name: Just Dottie
runners_data.note: True hold-up performer for R Mike Smith (same trainer as Follow Charlie), placed in the midfield map due to congestion at the rear; best form has come on Good ground over shorter, and Miss Becky Smith's 7lb claim helps, but the 19-day turnaround and modest form (five-run string without a win) limit expectations.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked eighth of ten on our figures, Just Dottie faces a stiff task here, though she returns on a quick turnaround of 19 days, has experience of today's going, and her third last time out offers a crumb of encouragement.

runners_data.name: Annie Agnew
runners_data.note: Genuinely wants to race prominently but the map has her in midfield due to pace congestion; 85-day absence is notable, and on Good ground she has only one win from nine similar-going runs — out of role and undercooked heading into this.
runners_data.comment: Yet to score in her last five starts, Annie Agnew nonetheless brings distance and going experience to the table, and our rating of 109 marks her out as a live threat off 156 lb; the main risk is a return from 85 days off.

runners_data.name: Struth
runners_data.note: Consistent backmarker for Russell/Scudamore, zero wins from ten runs on Good or Soft ground in the last five — the form string (55-666) tells its own story; Derek Fox is an experienced handler of hold-up horses but the raw material here is limited and the redistribution to midfield only worsens the tactical picture.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, with a sequence of three consecutive sixths the most damning evidence against him, Struth is ranked last on our figures here and is hard to fancy despite having run over today's trip and going before.

races.paceDynamic: Lets Mingle is the sole confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine rival to push them along, Jack Power's mount should be able to bowl along at a controlled, sustainable gallop over this 2m4f trip on Good ground at Perth. The prominent pack — Harry, Summergrounds, and Cosmic Soul — will sit just behind but none are natural pace-pressers, meaning Lets Mingle is unlikely to be seriously challenged for the lead and can dictate every yard. This single-pace, uncontested scenario strongly favours horses that can track the leader closely and pounce in the straight, rewarding prominent racers who avoid an energy-sapping early battle. The field holds more prominent-types than the map can accommodate — O'Faolains Glory and Annie Agnew are genuine prominent horses who have been pushed into midfield on the map; Lets Mingle and Harry are best-placed to actually lock down their natural early positions, with Summergrounds and Cosmic Soul fighting for the next slots.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lets Mingle Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Lets Mingle is allowed to bowl along at a steady gallop with no rival forcing the pace, setting a rhythm that favours those travelling just behind.
scenarios.body: Lets Mingle dictates a comfortable tempo throughout and the race turns into a test of who has tracked most efficiently; prominent closers arriving fresh off the pace are best positioned.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely steady enough to compress the field and a true hold-up runner finds a clear run in the straight.
scenarios.body: Dream's Ka — with solid Good-ground form (six wins/places from ten on similar) and a young, progressive profile — is the likeliest beneficiary, while Follow Charlie's recent course-distance win gives hope.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Increases, Prominent Battle
scenarios.trigger: If O'Faolains Glory or Annie Agnew push forward from their mapped midfield positions and inject unexpected early pressure.
scenarios.body: The race quickens sooner than anticipated, burning off rivals and leaving only horses who settled calmly in contention; Cosmic Soul's four wins from eleven Good-ground runs and Brian Hughes in the saddle make it a prime beneficiary of any pace collapse at the front.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Handicap Lottery, Compressed Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the steady pace produces a sprint finish with the entire field still in contention at the second-last hurdle.
scenarios.body: Horses with high TopSpeed and sharp finishing ability come to the fore in a bunched cavalry charge; the even handicap weights make this a genuine lottery but Garde Des Champs — consistent in form (three placings from last five) — and Follow Charlie have the tactical flexibility to profit.

watchPoints.text: Watch Lets Mingle's jumping — if Jack Power's 5lb claimer makes even one significant error at a hurdle while leading unchallenged, the rhythm that makes this horse's front-running style effective is immediately compromised and the race opens up.
O'Faolains Glory's 146-day absence means fitness is unproven; if it pushes forward from its unfavourable map position and fades, it could cause interference for horses tracking prominently behind.

Brian Hughes on Cosmic Soul is a significant booking — if Hughes elects to improve earlier than expected, it could inject pace into the mid-race and disrupt Lets Mingle's controlled gallop more than the pace map anticipates.

Annie Agnew and O'Faolains Glory are both prominent types mapped to midfield due to overcrowding — watch the early stages to see whether either forces forward, as this could alter the race tempo materially from what the single-front-runner shape predicts.

Dream's Ka's young age (4) and hold-up style mean Ryan Mania will need a clean passage entering the straight — in an 11-runner field on a circuit like Perth, traffic can be a decisive factor for hold-up horses making late ground.

races.name: Malcolm Group Handicap Hurdle Race

runners_data.name: Dolly Dior
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with a strong recent record on good ground (5/5 sim-going appearances, one win, two places), ridden by Brian Hughes and dropping back slightly in distance from 20f — a genuine fit for this race shape if she can track Burgundy Man efficiently from the front rank.|
runners_data.comment: Dolly Dior appeals as a serious threat, winning two starts back and filling the runner-up spot last time out, with experience of today's going working in her favour; the concern is whether 168 lb blunts her finishing effort.

runners_data.name: October Hill
runners_data.note: David Pipe-trained prominent type with excellent good-ground course form, wearing a tongue-tie; the 5lb claim of Rian Corcoran is a practical asset over 3m, and his record of seven places from ten similar-going runs marks him as a durable, consistent stalker.|
runners_data.comment: Runners-up last time out and a winner three starts back, October Hill arrives in fine form and fitness on 20 days' rest, with experience of today's trip and conditions working in her favour at 166 lb.

runners_data.name: Just Oot
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning from a significant 427-day absence for Susan Corbett; the layoff is a major concern at this trip, and while he placed at 21f on good ground in the past, the fitness question mark makes him hard to rely on despite a reasonable staying profile.|
runners_data.comment: A lengthy absence of 427 days is the obvious concern for Just Oot, who was runner-up two starts back yet is winless in his last four outings; he has experience of today's going, but carrying 165 lb after such a layoff makes this a tough ask.

runners_data.name: Dalileo
runners_data.note: An 11-year-old hold-up specialist who has won twice at 24f on good going in recent form, giving him strong credentials for this 3m trip; Callum Bewley takes the ride and his good-ground record (3 wins, 6 places from 15 runs) is the standout stamina case in the field.|
runners_data.comment: Dalileo won his last two starts and has experience of today's distance and going, but he carries a hefty 164 lb and is ranked seventh of eleven, which tempers expectations despite the in-form profile.

runners_data.name: Broken Ice
runners_data.note: Trainer John McConnell is in good form (2/31 in 14 days) and the horse handles good ground, but as a natural hold-up type pushed into a midfield mapping position due to field congestion, it will race out of role — discount its chance in scenarios requiring a deep late run.|
runners_data.comment: Broken Ice rates the pick of this field on our figures and has experience of today's trip and conditions, making him a strong candidate despite carrying a hefty 163 lb; the concern is that he has been winless in his last five starts, including an unplaced effort last time out.

runners_data.name: Ceol Draiochta
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner with a modest profile on good ground (no wins or places from 8–10 sim-going runs) and a history of pulled-up and unseated finishes; Ryan Mania's experience helps but the form figures offer little encouragement over this extended trip.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts and twice pulled up in that spell, Ceol Draiochta faces an uphill task here; experience over today's going is a modest plus, but a burden of 163 lb tests his resolve further.

runners_data.name: Drumlee Myth
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse forced into a mapped midfield position by the density of rear-runners in this field; won at 22f on good ground last time out which is encouraging for the trip, but racing ahead of his natural position will compromise his chance.|
runners_data.comment: Drumlee Myth arrives on the back of a win last time out and has already shown he handles today's going, making him a genuine threat at the weights carrying 151 lb; the worry is whether he can back up that victory after a run of inconsistent efforts before it.

runners_data.name: Magic Gloves
runners_data.note: Prominent-style runner trained by Lucinda Russell and Michael Scudamore, wearing a tongue-tie and returning after 69 days off; the recent form figures of 0-0 and a string of 8th-10th place finishes on good and soft ground suggest he is out of form at this level.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked ninth of eleven on our figures, Magic Gloves faces a stiff ask here; she has going experience in her favour and two fourth-place finishes offer faint encouragement, but a 69-day absence and a burden of 145 lb make her difficult to fancy.

runners_data.name: Fortunes Dawn
runners_data.note: Prominent runner for William Young Jnr who has placed at 20f on good ground recently; with only three historical runs to assess and a modest OR of 80, he is an unknown quantity over 3m but his natural style suits a sustainable-pace scenario.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked tenth of eleven on our figures, Fortunes Dawn faces a stiff ask here, though she does return from a 34-day break with a third last time out and experience of today's going in her favour.

runners_data.name: Burgundy Man
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner in this race and the pace-setter by default; trainer R Mike Smith has had one winner in 13 runs over 14 days and the horse wears tongue-tie and a hood, but a record of no wins and five places at 24f suggests he may be passed in the final stages even from the front.|
runners_data.comment: Burgundy Man has run over today's trip and going but his recent record is a concern, with two pulled-up efforts in his last five starts and winless throughout; the 44-day absence adds further uncertainty, though a rating of 95 gives connections reason for quiet optimism.

runners_data.name: Quinnfinity
runners_data.note: Flagged as a horse that fades in the finish — a significant concern over 3m — and a natural hold-up type displaced into a midfield map position; only three career runs on record and a form string of P-P8 makes this a very risky proposition at this distance and in this company.|
runners_data.comment: Quinnfinity has pulled up in two of her last three starts and finished eighth in the other, making her very hard to fancy here, though she has run over today's going before and 44 days off may have freshened her up.

races.paceDynamic: Burgundy Man is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 11-runner 3m handicap hurdle and, crucially, faces no genuine pace rival to push him along — he can dictate a comfortable, controlled gallop from the outset on good ground at Perth. With Dolly Dior, October Hill, Magic Gloves, and Fortunes Dawn all carrying prominent style profiles, there will be early jockeying for position behind the leader, but none of these represents a genuine pace threat to Burgundy Man's lead. The field contains an unusually high concentration of hold-up horses — Broken Ice, Drumlee Myth, and Quinnfinity are all natural rearward runners redistributed into the midfield on the map because the true back of the field is overcrowded; those three are unlikely to get their preferred deep position and will race closer than ideal. This sustainable, uncontested pace shape over an extended 3m trip strongly favours prominent-to-midfield stalkers who can track the leader without burning energy early and pick off a tiring Burgundy Man in the home straight, rather than genuine closers who will find insufficient pace injection to reel the field in from far back.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Burgundy Man Controls, Stalkers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Burgundy Man sets a comfortable, uncontested gallop and the prominent horses track efficiently to pounce from the second-last hurdle.
scenarios.body: Burgundy Man dictates a genuine but manageable pace over 3m, and the horses who have tracked him throughout — fresh enough from their prominent berth — outrun him from two out on good ground. Dolly Dior and October Hill, both proven prominent operators on good going, are the chief beneficiaries of this dominant race shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Grind It Out
scenarios.trigger: If the initial grouping behind Burgundy Man becomes congested and a steady war of attrition unfolds through the final mile.
scenarios.body: The sustained 3m trip on good ground stretches the field into a procession, rewarding horses with the best stamina credentials in the prominent-to-midfield bracket. Dalileo, who has won twice at 24f on good ground recently, and Fortunes Dawn, who has course-appropriate form at the trip, come through a tiring pack late.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Land Late Blow
scenarios.trigger: If Burgundy Man sets a stronger pace than expected and the race develops sufficient tempo to bring closers into play from the home turn.
scenarios.body: In this less likely shape, the redistributed hold-up types — Broken Ice and Dalileo — manage to find daylight from their forced midfield positions and generate a late run. However, given that Broken Ice and Drumlee Myth are racing out of their natural role, this scenario depends on an uncharacteristic pace injection that Burgundy Man alone is unlikely to generate.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Front Pair Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Burgundy Man bowls along unchallenged and simply refuses to be caught, with the field behind strung out and unable to mount a challenge.
scenarios.body: Burgundy Man, given a soft lead throughout and never asked a serious question until too late, stays on doggedly to the line with one prominent tracker unable to reel him in. October Hill, who is proven at the trip and goes well on good ground, is best placed of the chasers to take second but cannot collar the front-runner.

watchPoints.text: Burgundy Man's uncontested lead is the defining tactical factor — watch whether Brian Hughes on Dolly Dior or Peter Kavanagh on Fortunes Dawn attempts to press him early, because any increase in pace could dramatically alter which profiles benefit.|

Dalileo's stamina credentials at 3m on good ground are the strongest in the field given two recent wins at 24f, but Callum Bewley will need to navigate through a congested midfield pack — any traffic problems turning for home will cost him dearly.|

Just Oot's 427-day absence for Susan Corbett is a significant red flag in a 3m handicap hurdle — watch for early signs of a horse short of peak fitness, particularly in the final mile where stamina reserves are tested.|

Broken Ice, Drumlee Myth, and Quinnfinity are all natural hold-up horses racing ahead of their preferred position due to field congestion — watch whether any of them drops out quickly from midfield if the pace is insufficiently strong to suit a late run.|

The good ground is consistent throughout the card at Perth and there is no sign of drying that would inconvenience any runner, but watch for Fortunes Dawn, who has only ever run on good going — any ground deterioration late in the afternoon could matter if this race is re-scheduled or going description updated.|

races.name: Scone Estates Stone Of Destiny Handicap Hurdle Race (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: The Last Cloud
runners_data.note: Prominent racer returning from 168 days off and all five recent runs have been on Soft or Standard ground, so this Good surface is a genuine positive shift — but the long layoff for the Patrick Neville yard, which is 0/5 in the past 14 days, raises fitness concerns; will need to handle early pace pressure from the inside rail.
runners_data.comment: Third twice in his last three completed starts and a winner five starts back, The Last Cloud brings solid recent form to the table and has experience of today's distance and going; the chief concern is a 168-day absence, and that pull-up last time cannot be ignored.

runners_data.name: Filibustering
runners_data.note: Back-to-back wins on Good ground over this exact 2m trip, Harry Derham's yard in fair form, and the tongue strap applied — this is the standout pace angle in the race and most likely to control proceedings from the front; the key question is whether three-wide pace competition eventually takes its toll.
runners_data.comment: Filibustering arrives on the back of three consecutive wins and, despite 48 days off the track, that progressive profile earns him preference here; he has run over today's trip and going before, and 168 lb is the one thing to respect.

runners_data.name: Squeezebox
runners_data.note: Tom Lacey's hold-up specialist has an exceptional record on Good ground (10 from 15 similar-going runs) and has won over this trip and course configuration — settled off a contested pace, this is exactly the scenario that suits its style, and the headgear (hood and tongue strap) suggests it is primed.
runners_data.comment: Squeezebox arrives with three wins in his last five starts and has experience of both today's trip and conditions, giving him every chance to go well again; the 158 lb burden is the one factor connections will be watching closely.

runners_data.name: Medieval Gold
runners_data.note: Patrick Neville's prominent racer returns after 172 days and has run exclusively on Soft, making this Good ground debut a significant unknown; Derek Fox takes the ride and the horse has placed form at the trip, but the combination of layoff and untested surface is a material concern.
runners_data.comment: Medieval Gold shaped with plenty of encouragement when third two starts back and a winner three starts back, and his experience over today's trip is a solid asset at 156 lb; the chief concern is a 172-day absence.

runners_data.name: Fidendum
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner with a strong Good-ground profile (7 from 9 similar-going runs) but is handled by a claimer (Nick Slatter, 3lb), which matters when trying to dictate terms against Filibustering — likely to be pressed hard early and may find the pace contest costly in the final 2f.
runners_data.comment: Twice a winner in his last four starts, with a third sandwiched in between, though a refusal four starts back raises questions about consistency; has run over today's trip and going, and 41 days off the track is a minor query at 155 lb.

runners_data.name: Nap Hand
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer with a consistent placed record at 2m on Good ground; the 5lb claimer Fern O'Brien is a notable booking for Chris Gordon's yard, and the trainer has 1 win from 2 in the past 14 days — should get a genuine pace to aim at and is a realistic beneficiary of a hard gallop.
runners_data.comment: Consistent without a win in recent starts, Nap Hand has back-to-back second-place finishes and has run over today's trip and going, yet 150 lb is a stiff ask and his ranking fifth of eight on our ratings suggests he faces a tough task bridging the gap.

runners_data.name: Scriabin
runners_data.note: Third confirmed front-runner, last won on Good ground over this trip and has a solid record racing prominently; Lucinda Russell and Michael Scudamore's dual-trainer setup brings course familiarity, but Scriabin is most likely to be the sacrificial pace horse if Filibustering is sharper away.
runners_data.comment: Ranked seventh of eight on our figures, Scriabin is hard to fancy despite carrying 149 lb off an official mark of 110, and 44 days off the track adds a fitness query, though he does arrive on the back of a win last time out and has run over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Pure Gold
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up type whose true pattern is arriving late — mapped into midfield here because the race holds more closers than the visual structure shows, but the STYLE_FIT flag is valid; a 0/0 trainer record in the 14-day window and the lowest OR in the field (104) mean its chance is best tempered accordingly.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Pure Gold faces a stiff ask here; she has run over today's trip and going before, and a third last time out at least suggests she retains some ability.

races.paceDynamic: Filibustering, Fidendum, and Scriabin are all confirmed front-runners over this 2m trip at Perth on Good ground, making a strong, honest gallop from the outset virtually certain — there is no scenario where this race crawls. With three horses likely to contest the lead from the off, the pace will be genuine rather than manufactured, and the stamina of every participant will be thoroughly examined before the final flight. Hold-up runners Squeezebox and Nap Hand are best placed to exploit a contested lead ahead of them, while prominent types The Last Cloud and Medieval Gold must either take a pull or burn more energy than ideal fighting for position in the early stages. The field contains more front-running and prominent types than can all get their natural position — Filibustering, with the strongest recent form and Good-ground course profile, is most likely to actually control the race from the front, with Scriabin and Fidendum most likely to be pushed into a less comfortable contested lead or early prominent berth. This race shape firmly favours patient hold-up or midfield horses with proven stamina on Good ground who can pick up the pieces in the final stages.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Lead Burns Them
scenarios.trigger: If Filibustering, Fidendum, and Scriabin fight for supremacy and collectively force a relentless gallop that saps the leaders early.
scenarios.body: The pace war drains the front-runners before the last, leaving the race wide open for closers to sweep through; horses who settled off the pace conserve enough to challenge meaningfully at the business end.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: One Front-Runner Breaks Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Filibustering uses superior class and Good-ground form to get a clear lead early and controls the gallop at a sustainable rhythm.
scenarios.body: With only one horse truly dictating and the others sucked along at a manageable pace, Filibustering's strong recent form profile — including back-to-back wins — gives it a decisive stamina advantage over rivals who worked harder to match its early stride.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Outstay All
scenarios.trigger: If the contested gallop is fierce enough to leave every front-runner spent and hold-up horses unleash late runs from well off the pace.
scenarios.body: Squeezebox, with an outstanding record on Good ground and consistent form over this exact trip and surface, is perfectly suited to arriving late; Nap Hand's consistency at 2m on Good also fits this outcome.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If the leaders collectively ease off — implausible but possible — allowing a prominent hold-to-race horse to lead without burning energy.
scenarios.body: Medieval Gold or The Last Cloud, both comfortable travelling prominently, could profit from a falsely run race that rewards positional intelligence over raw stamina; however, the three confirmed front-runners make this the least likely shape in this field.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Filibustering, Fidendum, and Scriabin all break sharply — if all three contest the lead simultaneously in the first 2f, the resulting pace war is likely to leave all three compromised before the last and elevates Squeezebox and Nap Hand significantly.

Fidendum's use of a 3lb claimer (Nick Slatter) against a more experienced front-runner in Filibustering could prove costly if Fidendum cannot dictate naturally and is instead pushed wide or into an uncomfortably aggressive early position.

The Last Cloud and Medieval Gold are both returning from long layoffs (168 and 172 days respectively) for the same trainer (Patrick Neville, 0/5 in 14 days) — monitor market moves at the off; if either drifts materially, fitness concerns are likely already priced in by connections.

Pure Gold's redistribution from hold-up to mapped midfield reflects a crowded back-end — if the pace is fierce enough to compress the field, Pure Gold may genuinely struggle to find clear daylight in the straight despite the Good-ground surface suiting it on paper.

Squeezebox has an outstanding Good-ground record and was last seen finishing third 28 days ago at this trip — the freshness angle combined with the tongue strap and hood combination from Tom Lacey's yard suggests a horse ready to peak at this moment.

races.name: Brooks Macdonald Handicap Steeple Chase

runners_data.name: Shantou Show
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse carrying top weight of 168lbs with headgear (tongue-tie/pad) and only two placed efforts from 12 sim-going runs; at 10yo and off 24 days, the weight burden looks prohibitive in a contested-pace scenario over 3m.
runners_data.comment: Shantou Show shaped with promise when third two starts back and has run over today's trip and going, while our rating of 112 puts him right in the mix here; the concern is a pulled-up effort last time out.

runners_data.name: Button Rock
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who won over 20f on Good going (1/20f/GOO) and has solid sim-going form (4/7, 1W1P); Derek Fox is a sharp jockey for this type of race and 44 days off a 6yo should not be a major concern — well positioned to sit just off the pace leaders.
runners_data.comment: Button Rock bounces back to winning form on his return from 44 days off, showing recent going experience and carrying 166 lb admirably, though that burden is the chief concern for a horse who has mixed results in his last five starts.

runners_data.name: Le Malin
runners_data.note: Versatile but naturally hold-up inclined 12yo with a recent win over 20f on Good (1/20f/GOO) and strong place record in sim-going (6/12, 1W4P); amateur jockey Mr N McParlan (3) adds a small negative, but Le Malin's class and course-form profile make him a factor if the pace softens the front two.
runners_data.comment: Third last time out after winning two starts back, Le Malin arrives on a sharp 26-day turnaround with recent distance and going experience in his favour, and his profile looks well-suited to conditions here under 166 lb.

runners_data.name: Edgewell
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who has won twice on Good going and twice over 26f, with a blinkers headgear flag that underlines his need to be prominent; his sim-going dominance (10/15, 4W7P) is the strongest in the field and he must be respected as the likely pace controller.
runners_data.comment: Edgewell arrives on the back of back-to-back wins, which is the obvious draw, though a pulled-up run three starts back is a concern; he has run over today's trip and going before, and 36 days off the track leaves fitness a mild question mark at 164 lb.

runners_data.name: Collingham
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse pushed to midfield on the pace map because the field is rear-heavy; the visor aids concentration but STYLE_FIT of 0.93 flags he is racing out of role, and his recent form (P30-P4) and moderate sim-going record (13/15) mean he needs chaos in front to feature.
runners_data.comment: Collingham has run over today's trip and going, carries 161 lb off an official mark of 93, and our rating of 127 ranks him top of seven — yet two pulled-up runs in his recent form are the obvious concern for a gelding yet to score in his last five starts.

runners_data.name: Mcgregors Charge
runners_data.note: Front-runner fitted with tongue-tie who will press Edgewell early, but OR 79 and a form string of PP7-54 suggest he is likely to capitulate before the final mile; his role is primarily to force the pace rather than win, and Polly Gundry's T14 record of 0/0 offers no recent confidence.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, with two pulled-up efforts among them, Mcgregors Charge is hard to fancy despite a rating of 91 and experience over today's distance and going; the modest improvement in form latterly offers faint encouragement, but he faces an uphill task from this position in the rankings.

runners_data.name: Ballydangan
runners_data.note: True hold-up type returning from a lengthy 149-day absence, which is a significant flag at this level; STYLE_FIT 0.91 confirms he is out of his natural running position, and while he has won on Soft and placed on Good, the layoff and repositioning make him difficult to recommend.
runners_data.comment: Pulled up in two of his last four starts and absent for nearly five months, Ballydangan is hard to fancy at the foot of our rankings, though he has run over today's trip and going and a win does feature in recent starts.

races.paceDynamic: Edgewell and Mcgregors Charge are the two confirmed front-runners and will contest the early lead over the 3m trip on Good ground at Perth, creating an honest, pressured gallop from the outset rather than a false-pace scenario. Edgewell has the stronger recent form and superior sim-going record (10/15, 4W7P) and is likely to dominate the pace battle, with Mcgregors Charge applying pressure but unlikely to wrest control given his more modest profile (OR 79, form PP7-54). This contested early pace over 3m on Good turf will string the field out and favour horses who can travel smoothly in the slipstream without burning energy early, rewarding prominent stalkers and strong-travelling hold-up types with a genuine finishing kick. This field holds more hold-up horses than the map can accommodate at the rear — Collingham and Ballydangan are true closers who have been redistributed to midfield, and neither is likely to secure their natural position, meaning the realistic prominent slots behind the two leaders belong to Button Rock and potentially Le Malin. The race shape strongly favours a prominent, well-travelled racer who can pick off a tiring leader in the final mile — Button Rock and Le Malin, both mapped to sit handy or just off the pace, are the profiles that benefit most.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Pace, Stalker Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Edgewell and Mcgregors Charge fight for the lead and soften each other up, allowing a prominent tracker to pick them off in the straight.
scenarios.body: The two front-runners set a genuine gallop that stretches the field, and the horse sitting just off the pace in a prominent position conserves enough to challenge from the second-last fence; Button Rock, with a proven Good-ground win and prominent style, is ideally placed to pounce.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Leader Dominates Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Edgewell shakes off Mcgregors Charge early and dictates a controlled gallop, conserving enough to see out 3m strongly.
scenarios.body: Edgewell has won twice on Good going and twice over 26f, and if he neutralises the early threat from Mcgregors Charge he can control the tempo and quicken sufficiently when asked; his headgear (blinkers) and strong sim-going record (4W7P) support him seeing this out in front.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Storms Late
scenarios.trigger: If the contested pace is genuinely strong enough to bring hold-up types into play in the final half-mile despite their repositioning.
scenarios.body: Le Malin is the most likely beneficiary here given his class (12 top-5s in sim going) and a recent win over 20f on Good, though he is a natural hold-up type who will need the pace to have done serious damage to the leaders; Shantou Show is also capable on Good ground but faces age and weight concerns at 10yo/168lbs.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If early leaders go too fast and both capitulate, creating a scrambled finish that rewards a horse with enough tactical flexibility to switch gears.
scenarios.body: Collingham and Ballydangan, both true hold-up types pushed into midfield, would need chaos in front to get involved; their STYLE_FIT penalties and redistribution make this a low-probability route, and neither has the recent form to inspire confidence without ideal conditions.

watchPoints.text: Edgewell and Mcgregors Charge are on a collision course for the early lead — watch the opening half-mile to see if Edgewell establishes clear control or if a prolonged duel burns both front-runners out before the final mile.

Button Rock is the key prominent tracker to monitor; if Derek Fox settles him smoothly in second or third from the start, he is positioned to challenge from the second-last fence and his Going record makes him dangerous.

Le Malin's amateur rider (Mr N McParlan, 3lb claim) could be a factor in how well he is placed during the race — watch whether he travels fluently through the mid-section or gets outpaced as the pace quickens.

Ballydangan returns from 149 days off and should be watched in the early stages for any signs of rustiness at the fences — a jumping error or slow jumper could compromise his chance entirely in a strung-out field.
Collingham's visor fitting and true hold-up tendency mean he will be doing his best work late; if the front two do not fade, his chance of landing a blow from off the pace mapped to midfield is slim.

races.name: Scone Palace International Horse Trials National Hunt Flat Race (Conditional & Amateur Jockeys' Race) (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Captain Mainwaring
runners_data.comment: Captain Mainwaring has run over today's trip and going before and, despite being winless in recent starts, his rating of 92 ranks him among the leading players in this small field; the main concern is a 282-day absence.

runners_data.name: Dark Tide Rising
runners_data.comment: Unexposed and open to improvement, Dark Tide Rising has had a troubled recent campaign — pulling up, falling, and finishing fourth in his last three starts — but 98 days between runs suggests connections have taken their time, and he is yet to win but could still have more to offer.

runners_data.name: Downtown Nashville
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts, Downtown Nashville nonetheless has some encouraging form to his name — third last time out and a second four starts back — and has run over today's trip and going before; he carries 153 lb, but our top rating of 109 marks him as the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Game Shadow
runners_data.comment: Game Shadow shapes as a leading player on his rating of 96, and having run over today's trip and going he arrives with relevant experience; the chief concern is a 78-day absence and the fact he is yet to score in recent starts.
